newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery continues despite tax - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery continues despite tax - BOJ.

text.p: The Japanese economy continues to be on a recovery trend despite some fluctuations caused by an increase in the consumption tax on April 1, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in its quarterly economic outlook issued on Friday.
The real trade surplus has been on an increasing trend and the nominal current account surplus has also increased, albeit very moderately, the BOJ said in its spring report.

The report added that Japanese prices have stopped declining. Domestic wholesale prices rose in early April due to the rise in the national sales tax, but fundamentally prices are moving sideways or are increasing marginally.
Growth in money supply has declined somewhat compared with summer 1996, the BOJ said, adding that lending by private financial institutions continues to be lacklustre.
Japan's net exports are likely to continue rising, partly due to the yen's depreciation since mid-1995, the report said.
The extent of the negative effects of April's rise in the sales tax, including the reversal of the stepped-up demand that preceded the tax increase, has yet to be confirmed, it added.
Private demand has firmed, as production growth, income growth and the yen's depreciation augmented corporate profits and net exports, the report said.

It added that balance sheet adjustment pressures may continue to restrain economic recovery, so effective reforms of the economic structure are important in efforts to strengthen the basis for recovery.

The BOJ said it needs to carefully watch internal and external supply and demand, as well as exchange rates, because price differentials between Japan and other countries have narrowed and the general sense of weak supply-and-demand conditions for products has receded.
